name: Citizenship by Marriage to a Salvadoran Citizen

requirements.blocker_text: Constitution Article 92 and Ley Especial de Migracion y Extranjeria Article 156: a foreigner married to a Salvadoran citizen may naturalize after 2 years of residence in El Salvador, which can be accrued either before or after the marriage, combining temporary and definitive (permanent) residence periods. The constitutional text is explicitly gender-neutral, addressing both 'a foreigner [masculine] married to a Salvadoran [feminine]' and 'a foreigner [feminine] married to a Salvadoran [masculine]' by name. Fee: USD 700 (non-refundable); processing up to 9 months if documentation is complete. Foreign documents require apostille/authentication and Spanish translation.
requirements.fix_path: Marry a Salvadoran citizen and accumulate 2 years of residence in El Salvador (before or after the marriage), then apply with the USD 700 fee.

evidence_required.document: Proof of residence in El Salvador

outcome.physical_presence_requirement: 2 years, accruable before or after the marriage

sources.title: UNHCR Help El Salvador -- Constitution Article 92 and Migration Law Article 156, naturalization tracks including the 2-year foreign-spouse route
UN Women Global Gender Equality Constitutional Database -- Article 92's explicit gender-neutral phrasing for spousal naturalization

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (El Salvador). STATUS: DRAFT -- both sources are intergovernmental/academic-hosted (UNHCR, UN Women), tier 2, not El Salvador's own Official Gazette directly; despite a fee figure (USD 700) and 9-month timeline corroborated by a national newspaper (tier 4, not cited here as the primary source), no government-hosted primary text was independently confirmed in this build. GENUINE POSITIVE FINDING, EXPLICITLY GENDER-NEUTRAL: unlike several other marriage-citizenship routes built in this dataset (Syria, Guatemala's older framing, Zimbabwe), El Salvador's constitutional text names both directions explicitly -- a foreign man marrying a Salvadoran woman and a foreign woman marrying a Salvadoran man are treated identically. dual_citizenship_allowed set true: the elsalvador.com fee-schedule source (not independently re-verified here) noted no renunciation requirement for the related Central-American nationalization track, and no source reviewed found a renunciation requirement for this route either.
